en.text: Artemisia tridentata, commonly called big sagebrush, Great Basin sagebrush or simply sagebrush, is an aromatic shrub from the family Asteraceae.

es.text: La artemisa es una especie fanerógama de arbusto o pequeño árbol perteneciente a la familia Asteraceae.

fr.text: Artemisia tridentata, l'Armoise tridentée, est une espèce de plantes à fleurs de la famille des Asteraceae. Cet arbrisseau gris-argenté robuste, à fleurs jaunes, est typique de l'Amérique du Nord où il est désigné par le nom vernaculaire anglophone de « big sagebrush ».

id.text: Artemisia tridentata adalah semak aromatik dari keluarga Asteraceae yang tumbuh di wilayah kering hingga semi-kering, termasuk gurun, padang rumput, dan pegunungan dingin di Pegunungan Barat Amerika Utara. Spesies ini, bersama dengan semak Artemisia lainnya, merupakan tanaman dominan di sebagian besar Great Basin. Semak ini menyediakan makanan dan tempat tinggal bagi berbagai hewan termasuk wica, antelop, burung vireo abu-abu, kelinci kerdil, dan rusa bagal. Ekosistemnya menghadapi beberapa ancaman utama, seperti pemukiman manusia, konversi lahan menjadi pertanian, invasi tanaman asing, dan kebakaran hutan.

en.heading: Uses
en.text:
The Cahuilla used to gather large quantities of sagebrush seed and grind it to make flour. The main modern use is as firewood, with the wood's oils being particularly flammable.

■ Medicinal
The plant's active medicinal constituents include camphor, terpenoids, and tannins.
It is used as a herbal medicine by Native Americans throughout the Intermountain West of North America, most notably as a smudging herb. It is also used for preventing infection in wounds, stopping internal bleeding, and treating headaches and colds.
The Navajo use the vapors of sagebrush as a treatment for headache. The Okanagan and Colville people used sagebrush to smoke hides.
Among the Zuni people, an infusion of the leaves is used externally for body aches. The infusion is also taken as a cold medicine. It is also placed in shoes to treat athlete's foot, fissures between toes, and as a foot deodorant.
